sentence: Mum was happy to accept the invitation to the party.
hint: accept means to take or agree to something

sentence: Everyone went swimming except Zara, who had a cold.
hint: except means apart from

sentence: Kai kicked the ball over the garden fence.
hint: a ball is round and used in games

sentence: The toddler began to bawl when his ice cream fell on the floor.
hint: bawl means cry or shout loudly

sentence: A bright red berry was growing on the holly bush.
hint: a berry is a small, juicy fruit

sentence: Our dog likes to bury its bones in the garden.
hint: bury means hide in the ground; it sounds like berry

sentence: Dad pressed the brake to slow the car down.
hint: a brake slows or stops a vehicle

sentence: Be careful not to break the glass vase.
hint: break means smash, or a short rest

sentence: It is not fair that my brother always gets the biggest slice.
hint: fair means equal and right (or a funfair)

sentence: Mum paid the bus fare for both of us.
hint: a fare is the price of a journey

sentence: Please grate some cheese to sprinkle on the pizza.
hint: grate means rub food into tiny pieces

sentence: We had a great time at the seaside.
hint: great means very good or very big

sentence: Everyone let out a groan when the rain started again.
hint: a groan is a low sound of pain or annoyance

sentence: Our sunflower has grown taller than the fence.
hint: grown comes from grow

sentence: My new shoes rubbed the back of my heel.
hint: your heel is the back of your foot

sentence: The doctor said the cut on my knee would heal in a few days.
hint: heal means get better

sentence: Dad says he'll pick us up after the match.
hint: he'll is short for he will

sentence: The sailor tied a tight knot in the rope.
hint: a knot is tied in string or rope; the k is silent

sentence: We could not find our way through the thick fog.
hint: not makes a sentence negative

sentence: The postman delivered our mail before breakfast.
hint: mail is letters and parcels

sentence: The male peacock spreads out his beautiful tail feathers.
hint: male means a man or boy, or a boy animal

sentence: The main road into town was closed for repairs.
hint: main means most important or biggest

sentence: The horse shook its long, silky mane.
hint: a mane is the long hair on a horse's or lion's neck

sentence: Vegetarians do not eat meat or fish.
hint: meat is food that comes from animals

sentence: We will meet our new teacher on Monday.
hint: meet means come together

sentence: Priya won a gold medal for swimming.
hint: a medal is a prize you can wear

sentence: Please do not meddle with my model while the glue is drying.
hint: meddle means interfere

sentence: Leo missed the bus and had to walk to school.
hint: missed is the past tense of miss

sentence: A thick mist covered the hills, so we could not see far.
hint: mist is thin fog

sentence: After the noisy party, we enjoyed the peace and quiet of the garden.
hint: peace means calm, or no war

sentence: Would you like another piece of cake?
hint: a piece of pie: piece begins with pie

sentence: I would like a plain biscuit without any chocolate.
hint: plain means simple, or a wide flat area of land

sentence: The plane landed safely at the airport.
hint: a plane flies: it is short for aeroplane

sentence: Heavy rain fell all afternoon, so the match was cancelled.
hint: rain is water falling from clouds

sentence: The rider pulled gently on the rein to turn her horse.
hint: a rein is a strap for steering a horse

sentence: The first scene of the play takes place in a dark forest.
hint: a scene is part of a play, or a view

sentence: Have you seen my blue scarf anywhere?
hint: seen comes from see: I have seen

sentence: We walked down the aisle of the supermarket looking for rice.
hint: an aisle is a walkway between rows of seats or shelves

sentence: The ferry carried us across the sea to a small Scottish isle.
hint: an isle is an island; both have a silent s

sentence: For breakfast, I have a bowl of cereal with cold milk.
hint: cereal is a breakfast food made from grain

sentence: The story was shown as a serial, with a new episode every week.
hint: a serial is a story told in parts, like a series

sentence: Camels can survive for days in the hot, dry desert.
hint: a desert is a very dry place: one s

sentence: For dessert, we had strawberries and ice cream.
hint: dessert is pudding: two s's, like sweet stuff

sentence: Write a first draft of your story, then check it for mistakes.
hint: a draft is an early version of a piece of writing

sentence: A cold draught was blowing under the front door.
hint: a draught is a current of cold air

sentence: Our tent was farther from the river than we had thought.
hint: farther means at a greater distance

sentence: My father makes pancakes every Sunday.
hint: father means dad

sentence: Nobody guessed the answer to the riddle.
hint: guessed is the past tense of guess

sentence: Our special guest at the assembly was a real astronaut.
hint: a guest is a visitor

sentence: A herd of cows was grazing in the meadow.
hint: a herd is a large group of animals such as cows; heard comes from hear

sentence: The guide led us through the dark tunnels.
hint: led is the past tense of lead (show the way)

sentence: The old water pipes in the house were made of lead.
hint: lead (said like led) is a heavy grey metal

sentence: The sun rose early on the first morning of the holiday.
hint: morning is the early part of the day

sentence: In Victorian times, people wore black clothes when they were in mourning.
hint: mourning means grieving after someone has died

sentence: Our class sold cakes and made a profit of forty pounds.
hint: a profit is money you gain

sentence: In the old legend, a wise prophet warned the people about the flood.
hint: a prophet says what will happen in the future

sentence: The magpie tried to steal a shiny ring from the table.
hint: steal means take without permission

sentence: The new bridge is made of strong steel.
hint: steel is a strong metal

sentence: Be wary of the ice on the pond because it might be thin.
hint: wary means careful or cautious

sentence: After the long hike, the weary walkers sat down to rest.
hint: weary means very tired

sentence: A calculator is a useful device for checking answers.
hint: device is the noun, like advice

sentence: The children had to devise a plan to rescue the kitten.
hint: devise is the verb (to plan or invent), like advise

sentence: You need a licence to drive a car.
hint: licence is the noun in British English, like practice

sentence: The council will license the new market to open on Sundays.
hint: license is the verb in British English, like practise

sentence: In the old church, candles were burning on the altar.
hint: an altar is a holy table in a church or temple

sentence: The tailor had to alter my trousers because they were too long.
hint: alter means change

sentence: The climbers began their slow ascent of the steep mountain.
hint: ascent means going up, like ascend

sentence: The headteacher nodded her assent, so the trip could go ahead.
hint: assent means agreement

sentence: The bride wore a long bridal veil.
hint: bridal means to do with a bride

sentence: The rider fitted the bridle over the horse's head.
hint: a bridle is the set of straps on a horse's head for steering it

sentence: My teacher paid me a compliment about my neat handwriting.
hint: a compliment is praise: I like compliments

sentence: Warm custard is the perfect complement to apple crumble.
hint: a complement goes well with something and completes it

sentence: The plane began its descent towards the runway.
hint: descent means going down, like descend

sentence: The footballer was shown a yellow card for dissent after arguing with the referee.
hint: dissent means disagreement

sentence: A short warm-up should always precede a hard run.
hint: precede means come before: pre- means before

sentence: Passengers should now proceed to the boarding gate.
hint: proceed means go forward or carry on

sentence: The wizard's prophecy said that a young girl would save the kingdom.
hint: prophecy is the noun (a prediction), like advice

sentence: The fortune teller claimed that she could prophesy the future.
hint: prophesy is the verb (to predict), like advise
